title: U.S. House · South Dakota At-Large
area: Statewide, South Dakota (single at-large congressional district).

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Dusty Johnson (R) is not seeking re-election to the House and withdrew from this race, running instead for Governor of South Dakota in 2026. Marty Jackley, the sitting South Dakota Attorney General, defeated James Bialota 79.2%-20.8% in the June 2, 2026 Republican primary (Casey Crabtree and Dusty Johnson also withdrew from that primary). Nicole Gronli (also known as Nikki Gronli) advanced unopposed after South Dakota's Democratic primary was canceled. Jack Pittman (independent) did not make the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Marty Jackley
candidates.currentRole: Attorney General of South Dakota (2023-present; previously 2009-2019)

summary.text: Marty Jackley is the Republican nominee for South Dakota's open at-large House seat. A former private attorney and U.S. Attorney for South Dakota, he has been the state's Attorney General from 2009 to 2019 and again since 2023. He is running on public safety, border security and support for the Trump administration's agenda.

background.text: Raised in Sturgis, South Dakota, where he graduated from Sturgis High School in 1988.

Earned a bachelor's degree from the South Dakota School of Mines and Technology in 1992 (electrical engineering, according to his campaign website) and a law degree from the University of South Dakota in 1995. According to his campaign website, he then clerked for Chief Federal Judge Richard Battey.
Worked as a partner at the Rapid City firm Gunderson, Palmer, Nelson & Ashmore, LLP, and as a special assistant attorney general for South Dakota prosecuting controlled-substance felonies.

Served as U.S. Attorney for the District of South Dakota from 2006 to 2009; his campaign website says he was appointed and unanimously confirmed by the U.S. Senate and named Prosecutor of the Year in 2008.
Was appointed South Dakota Attorney General by Gov. Mike Rounds (R) on August 14, 2009, sworn in September 4, 2009, and elected in 2010 and 2014, serving until January 2019.
Ran for the Republican nomination for governor in 2018 and lost the June 5, 2018 primary.

According to his campaign website, he returned to private practice from 2019 to 2022 as a senior partner at his former firm, and served as State's Attorney for Jones and Haakon counties and as special prosecutor for the Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate.
Elected Attorney General again in 2022 and took office January 2, 2023; his term ends January 4, 2027, and he is not seeking re-election to that office.

According to his campaign website, he chaired the National Association of Attorneys General (2015), the Western Attorneys General and the National Attorneys General Alliance (2023-24), was named National Attorney General of the Year in 2016, and was elected president-elect of the national attorneys general association in December 2025.

His campaign website says his father, Mike Jackley, practiced law in Sturgis and served as Meade County State's Attorney, and that Jackley has a son and a daughter and spends family time at a farm near Vale and a ranch near Pierre.

priorities.text: Public safety: backing police, sheriffs and prosecutors, drawing on his career prosecuting violent crime as Attorney General.
Border and immigration: securing the border and "finishing the wall," citing his prosecution of drug traffickers.
Supporting the Trump administration's agenda, including securing the border and cutting taxes.

positions.summary: Calls for securing the border, finishing the border wall, and says he has prosecuted traffickers who bring drugs across it.
positions.quote: Secure the border, finish the wall, and let law enforcement do its job.

positions.summary: Says the right to keep and bear arms is not negotiable and cites an A+ rating from the NRA.
positions.quote: The right to keep and bear arms is not negotiable.

positions.summary: Says he will back police, sheriffs and prosecutors with the tools and respect they have earned.

candidates.name: Nicole Gronli

summary.text: Nicole (Nikki) Gronli is the Democratic nominee for South Dakota's open at-large House seat. She is a small-business owner and marketing professional who led USDA Rural Development in South Dakota from 2022 to 2025 and previously served as vice chair of the South Dakota Democratic Party. She says she is running to advocate for South Dakota and an economy that works for everyone.

background.text: According to a 2025 news report, she graduated from Brookings High School in 1991 and says she considers Brookings and Aurora jointly her home; she now lives in Dell Rapids.

Describes herself as a small-business owner with nearly 30 years of experience in marketing, communications and leadership; news coverage identifies her as president of the marketing company Flatlander Strategies.
Served as vice chair of the South Dakota Democratic Party, according to news coverage of her 2025 campaign announcement.

Led USDA Rural Development in South Dakota from 2022 to 2025 (state director under the Biden administration), overseeing investments in rural housing, broadband, infrastructure and community facilities.

Has served on Dakota State University's Cyber Security Industry Advisory Board, as president of the Department of Defense STARBASE board, and as an appointee to the Minnehaha County Housing and Redevelopment Commission board.
According to her campaign website, she and her husband, Brian, are parents and grandparents.

priorities.text: Says she is running to advocate for South Dakota and build "an economy that works for everyone."

candidates.researchNotes: Gronli's campaign site did not have an accessible detailed policy-positions page at the time of research (a linked "Priorities" page returned a 404); positions beyond her general economic message could not be documented from primary sources found.
